chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Baseer, and Bureyd al-Ijli, and al-Fudayl, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the cows: in every thirty cows, one Tabi' (one-year-old cow) is due, and there is nothing due for less than that; and in forty cows, one Musinnah (two-year-old cow) is due, and there is nothing due for what is between thirty and forty until it reaches forty. So when it reaches forty, then in it is one Musinnah, and there is nothing due for what is between forty and sixty. So when it reaches sixty, then in it are two Tabi' up to seventy. So when it reaches seventy, then in it is one Tabi' and one Musinnah up to eighty. So when it reaches eighty, then in every forty is one Musinnah up to ninety. So when it reaches ninety, then in it are three Tabi' (one-year-olds). So when it reaches one hundred and twenty, then in every forty is one Musinnah.

Then the cows are accounted for according to their ages. And there is nothing due on the 'Nayyif' (extra ten), nor on the fractions, nor on the 'Awilah' (working cows). Indeed, the Zakat is on the grazing herd. And whatever has not completed a year in the possession of its owner, there is nothing due upon it until the year passes over it. So when the year passes over it, it becomes obligatory upon it.
ai.seo_question: What is the Zakat rate for cattle according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the detailed nisab and distribution rules for Zakat on cattle, emphasizing that the obligation applies specifically to 'saimah' (grazing herds) rather than working animals. It highlights the Shia scholarly principle that the lunar year (hawl) must be completed in the owner's possession for the tax to become due, excluding fractional counts or non-grazing livestock.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara and Muhammad Bin Muslim and Abu Baseer, and Bureyd Al Ijaly, and Al Fuzayla, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> both having said regarding the cows:

‘In every thirty cows is one Tabi’e (baby cow) a year old, and there is nothing regarding less than that; and regarding forty cows, is a two year old cow, and there is nothing regarding what is between the thirty to the forty until it reaches forty. So when it does reach forty, so regarding these would be a two year old cow, and there would be nothing regarding what is between the forty up to the sixty.
So when it does reach the sixty, so regarding these would be two one-year olds up to seventy. So when it reaches seventy, so regarding these would be a one-year old and a two-year old up to eighty. So when it does reach eighty, so regarding every forty would be a two-year old up to ninety. So when it reaches ninety, so regarding these would be three one-year olds. So when it reaches one hundred and twenty and two hundred, so regarding every forty would be a two year old.

Then the cows would be returned (accounted) upon their ages. And there is nothing upon the in between, nor upon the fractions, nor upon the working cows, but rather, the charity (Zakāt) is upon the grazing ones. And everything upon which the year has not passed in the possession of its lord, so there is nothing upon it until the year passes by upon it. So when the year passes by upon it, it (Zakāt) would be Obligated upon it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah, Muhammad ibn Muslim, abu Basir, Burayd al-‘ljliy and al-Fudayl who have said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, and abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, have said, ‘

The amount of Zakat on cows is one Tabi‘ (a one year old cow) Hawliy for every thirty cows. Zakat is not due on less than this number of cows. Zakat on forty cows is one Musinnah (a young cow that is just growing teeth) Baqarah. Zakat is not due on what is between forty up to sixty. When it becomes sixty, Zakat is two Tabi‘ up to seventy. When it becomes seventy, Zakat is one Tabi‘ and one Musinnah up to eighty, in which case Zakat on every forty, is one Musinnah up to ninety in which case Zakat is three Tabi‘ Hawliy. When it becomes one hundred twenty, Zakat on every forty is one Musinnah;

and thereafter the cows are counted according to their ages. Zakat is not due on what is between two numbers. (It is like the case of camels) Zakat is not due on fractions or working cows. Zakat is obligatory only on grazing cows, which are not fed by the owner. Zakat is not due for cows on which one year has not passed. When one year passes, then Zakat is obligatory.”’
